title: AZ-900 · Describe cloud computing · Define cloud models

questions.category: Describe Cloud Concepts > Describe cloud computing
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Define cloud models
questions.question: Which statement best describes Public cloud?

options.text: Cloud infrastructure built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider and available to customers who purchase services
Ongoing spending for services consumed over time
Cloud pricing in which charges generally track actual service consumption
The ability to place services closer to users and design regional resilience without building your own worldwide datacenters

questions.explanation: Public cloud is cloud infrastructure built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider and available to customers who purchase services.

questions.category: Describe Cloud Concepts > Describe cloud computing
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Define cloud models
questions.question: In the context of this Microsoft Learn unit, what does Private cloud refer to?

options.text: Managed or hosted database capabilities delivered through a cloud platform
Removing resource instances when demand falls
An AZ-900 domain covering management, monitoring, cost, and governance and accounting for roughly 30–35% of the exam
A cloud environment dedicated to a single organization, offering greater control but typically greater cost and management responsibility

questions.explanation: Private cloud is a cloud environment dedicated to a single organization, offering greater control but typically greater cost and management responsibility.

questions.category: Describe Cloud Concepts > Describe cloud computing
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Define cloud models
questions.question: Which description correctly matches Hybrid cloud?

options.text: The ability to decide which workloads remain private and which use public-cloud capacity

An interconnected environment that combines private and public cloud resources
An AZ-900 domain covering management, monitoring, cost, and governance and accounting for roughly 30–35% of the exam

questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud is an interconnected environment that combines private and public cloud resources.

questions.category: Describe Cloud Concepts > Describe cloud computing

questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of Multicloud?

options.text: The use of services from two or more public cloud providers
Allocating more capacity than needed, which can create unnecessary cost
Compute resources that can be delivered as cloud services instead of requiring local physical servers
A model in which you pay for the IT resources you use and can release them when they are no longer needed

questions.explanation: Multicloud is the use of services from two or more public cloud providers.

options.text: An AZ-900 domain covering general cloud ideas and accounting for roughly 25–30% of the exam

questions.category: Describe Cloud Concepts > Describe cloud computing
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Define cloud models
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Public cloud: the use of services from two or more public cloud providers.
Hybrid cloud: a beginner-oriented series that introduces Azure services, cloud concepts, governance, and management.
Private cloud: a cloud environment dedicated to a single organization, offering greater control but typically greater cost and management responsibility.
Private cloud: the ability to provision and deprovision resources quickly without purchasing new datacenter hardware.
Public cloud: cloud infrastructure built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider and available to customers who purchase services.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Public cloud — cloud infrastructure built, controlled, and maintained by a third-party provider and available to customers who purchase services; and Private cloud — a cloud environment dedicated to a single organization, offering greater control but typically greater cost and management responsibility.
